title: Annual zoning by-law update for 2026
subtitle: Backyard units, private home daycares, bike lockers, setbacks, plus arena cold water ice and fleet electrification reports
overview: The committee recommended approving the City's annual zoning by-law update for both Zoning By-law 85-1 and Zoning By-law 2019-051 {{vote:m1}}. The update is a set of technical changes meant to add flexibility and clarity, especially for smaller infill housing such as additional dwelling units and townhouses.

Changes include a central set of rules for unobstructed walkways, new bicycle locker options, reduced minimum block widths for some townhouses, and a clearer overlay for the provincial rule that lets some properties meet a reduced share of required setbacks. The committee also recommended allowing private home daycares in any dwelling unit. A staff-proposed amendment fixed a missed change on setbacks beside common walls in the 2019-051 by-law. Council still has to adopt the recommendation.

The committee also discussed two information items, on cold water ice in City arenas and on fleet electrification. These were received for information and did not need a decision. Staff said a greenhouse gas study of arenas and a sustainable fleet transition strategy are under way.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving City-initiated amendment ZBA25/029/COK/SH to Zoning By-law 85-1 and Zoning By-law 2019-051, with no further public notice required.
The committee recommended amending the 2019-051 by-law to include the common-wall townhouse side yard setback wording from Appendix C, which staff had initially left out.
The recommendation centralizes unobstructed walkway rules, adds slope and length limits, and allows some steps in side yards.
The recommendation allows private home daycares in any dwelling unit and removes the 25% limit on the share of the unit used.
The recommendation adds a wedge-shaped bicycle locker option and allows reduced minimum block widths for some townhouses and multiple dwellings.

debate: One councillor asked about the new bicycle lockers, which fit about 85% of bikes. Staff said larger bikes, such as extra-large frames and some e-bikes, may not fit and would need a broader study than an annual update.

Councillors asked whether the new walkway rules could add cost or delay. Staff said the new 8% maximum slope came from emergency services concerns about reaching units with equipment or a stretcher, and steps can be used where a slope is too steep.
Several councillors supported the update as a way to remove barriers to missing-middle housing and backyard units. Staff said they consulted a development liaison committee and small builders.

The chair raised the 40% driveway-width limit in central neighbourhoods, compared with 50% elsewhere. Staff said a multi-department group is reviewing driveway and parking rules, with changes expected in a later update.

On the information items, councillors asked about scaling cold water ice and fleet electrification. Staff said a greenhouse gas study of arenas and a fleet strategy that includes battery storage are under way.
